## Results

### The first release

![**The first model's outputs at the first release.**
(A) Cumulative infections at the cut-off from the export-based and death-based methods of McCabe et al., each scenario a point with the headline scenario filled and its 90% interval as a line.
The same panel carries their death-based method reproduced at fixed inputs and the joint fit to two cut-offs, each a median with a 90% interval and a 50% interval on the later fit only.
(B) Cumulative infections at the cut-off from the joint model fitted to each stream alone, with the fitted count in the label, and to all four streams, as 30%, 60% and 90% intervals.
(C) The constant-growth latent curve of cumulative infections as the median with 50% and 90% bands, with the two fitted DRC counts marked and the seeding-date density beneath.
The release carries no medians for the single-stream fits, so (B) shows intervals only.](figures/fig-first){#fig-first}

At the first release the joint posterior of cumulative infections sat above both headline scenarios of McCabe et al. [@mccabe2026], a median of {{< meta first_release_median >}} (90% interval {{< meta first_release_interval90 >}}) against {{< meta mccabe_headline_exports >}} and {{< meta mccabe_headline_deaths >}} (@fig-first A).
The single-stream fits overlapped one another and the joint fit, with the suspected-death fit the narrowest and the fit to deaths among exports the widest (@fig-first B).
The latent curve placed most of the seeding density in the months before the first report, and both fitted DRC counts sat below the median curve at the cut-off (@fig-first C).

### Outbreak size and dynamics at the release analysed

![**The joint model at the release analysed.**
(A) Posterior daily symptom onsets nationally as the median with 30%, 60% and 90% bands, above the confirmed cases reported per day as points, with the dashed line the data cut-off.
(B) The reproduction number at the cut-off for each province and nationally, as 30%, 60% and 90% intervals, against a dashed line at one.
(C) Ascertainment by stream as 30% and 90% intervals, with the median where the release carries it and the prior median as an open diamond, for suspected cases, exported cases, the fraction of suspects tested and the onset reports.
(D) New confirmed cases and deaths in the seven days to each target date as points, with forecasts for the week to the cut-off and the week after as medians with 30% and 90% intervals.
The release carries no median for the provincial reproduction numbers or the fraction tested, and the onset reports have no single prior median, so those markers are absent.](figures/fig-current){#fig-current width=85%}

At the data cut-off of the release analysed the joint model estimated {{< meta cumulative_infections_median >}} cumulative infections (90% interval {{< meta cumulative_infections_interval90 >}}), {{< meta ratio_infections_to_confirmed >}} times the {{< meta confirmed_cases_at_cutoff >}} confirmed cases reported by then.
The posterior daily onsets rose over the first two months of reporting, levelled off from July, and eased towards the cut-off (@fig-current A).
The national reproduction number at the cut-off was {{< meta rt_cutoff_median >}} (90% interval {{< meta rt_cutoff_interval90 >}}), with {{< meta rt_cutoff_prob_above_one >}} of draws above one (@fig-current B).
The daily growth rate at the cut-off was {{< meta growth_rate_interval90 >}} (90% interval), the case-fatality ratio was {{< meta cfr_median >}} (90% interval {{< meta cfr_interval90 >}}) and the first infection was placed {{< meta outbreak_age_days_interval90 >}} days before the cut-off (90% interval).
Every provincial reproduction number straddled one at the cut-off, and the probability that it was above one was {{< meta ituri_rt_prob_above_one >}} in Ituri, {{< meta nord_kivu_rt_prob_above_one >}} in Nord-Kivu, {{< meta haut_uele_rt_prob_above_one >}} in Haut-Uele and {{< meta other_rt_prob_above_one >}} in the remaining provinces (@fig-current B).

The posterior on suspected-case ascertainment moved below its prior median of {{< meta suspected_ascertainment_prior_median >}} to {{< meta suspected_ascertainment_median >}} (90% interval {{< meta suspected_ascertainment_interval90 >}}), and export ascertainment moved from {{< meta export_ascertainment_prior_median >}} to {{< meta export_ascertainment_median >}} (90% interval {{< meta export_ascertainment_interval90 >}}) (@fig-current C).
The 90% interval of the fraction of suspects tested, {{< meta tested_fraction_interval90 >}}, started at its prior median of {{< meta tested_fraction_prior_median >}}, and the onset-report ascertainment was {{< meta onset_ascertainment_interval90 >}} (90% interval) (@fig-current C).

The fit that produced these estimates passed the convergence gate, with a maximum R-hat of {{< meta max_rhat >}}, a minimum bulk effective sample size of {{< meta min_ess_bulk >}} and a divergent-transition count of {{< meta n_divergent >}} over {{< meta sampler_chains >}} chains of {{< meta sampler_draws >}} draws.
The forecast made at the previous release gave {{< meta forecast_validation_confirmed_cases_median >}} new confirmed cases (90% interval {{< meta forecast_validation_confirmed_cases_interval90 >}}) and {{< meta forecast_validation_confirmed_deaths_median >}} new confirmed deaths (90% interval {{< meta forecast_validation_confirmed_deaths_interval90 >}}) for the week to the cut-off (@fig-current D).
The reports carried {{< meta observed_confirmed_cases_validation_week >}} cases and {{< meta observed_confirmed_deaths_validation_week >}} deaths over that week, so both streams fell below the 90% interval of the forecast (@fig-current D).

The release before the one analysed did not converge and was published with a convergence warning.
Convergence was restored at the next release, and the released median stayed inside the interval of the release that failed (@fig-journey C). <!-- VERIFY: agent-only account; news v2.0.0 note and PR 745; the release was published with the failure unnoticed and the CI convergence gate followed -->

### Estimate evolution across releases

![**The development journey by release.**
Every panel shares one date axis, with each release tag a vertical line labelled in the strip above and the three model versions as background bands.
(A) Lines of model and test code between tags, with the number of fitted streams as a dashed step on the right axis.
(B) Commits per week from human, agent and other accounts, stacked, with merged pull requests per week as a line.
(C) The released estimate of cumulative infections as the median with its 90% interval at each release's data cut-off on a log scale, with the data events beneath coloured by whether a human decision followed.
(D) Joint gradient time from the benchmark records, open markers before and filled after the same pull request, one pull request recorded only before its change, and the single recorded fit wall-clock as a diamond whose height carries no value.
Tags without a results release are absent from (C).](figures/fig-journey){#fig-journey width=75%}

The released estimate rose by more than an order of magnitude, from {{< meta first_release_median >}} at the first release to {{< meta last_release_median >}} at the last tagged release (@fig-journey C).
The largest step came with the move to situation-report increments and the laboratory model, where the median rose by a factor of {{< meta closed_form_step_ratio >}} between the last two releases of the closed-form model.
The estimate then fell at the release after the isolation step and again at the release after the local peak that followed, before rising over the remaining renewal releases (@fig-journey C).
Over the same window the number of fitted streams rose from four to eleven, most commits came from the agent account, and the recorded joint gradient time fell across the benchmarked pull requests (@fig-journey A, B and D).
Under the provincial model the two released estimates plateaued, and the release analysed, which postdates the last version tag and is not drawn, sat close to them at {{< meta cumulative_infections_median >}}.

### Forecast evaluation

![**Evaluation against persistence, single-stream fits and published estimates.**
(A) The continuous ranked probability score of the joint one-week-ahead forecast relative to persistence, by stream and release cut-off on a log scale, with a dashed parity line, hollow markers for backfilled releases and a strip marking 90% coverage.
Scores run only to the last cut-off drawn, so the provincial releases and the release analysed are unscored.
(B) Cumulative infections to the cut-off of the release analysed from the joint and each single-stream fit, as medians with 30%, 60% and 90% intervals, on a log scale.
(C) The geographic-spread and back-calculation scenarios of McCabe et al. at their three cut-offs as means with 95% confidence intervals, against the joint fit frozen at the two later cut-offs.
(D) The central, low and high projections of Chamla et al. with 90% prediction intervals, the joint fit frozen at their calibration date and drawn both there and at the week-12 date, and the observed confirmed series.
The frozen joint in (C) carries no median and has no fit at the first cut-off.](figures/fig-evaluation){#fig-evaluation}

The joint one-week-ahead forecast scored worse than persistence on most stream-release pairs, beating the baseline on {{< meta skill_pairs_beat >}} of {{< meta skill_pairs_total >}} pairs overall and on {{< meta skill_pairs_beat_live >}} of {{< meta skill_pairs_total_live >}} at the live releases (@fig-evaluation A).
By stream it beat persistence on {{< meta skill_confirmed_cases >}} releases for confirmed cases, {{< meta skill_confirmed_deaths >}} for confirmed deaths, {{< meta skill_isolation_beds >}} for isolation beds, {{< meta skill_onset_reports >}} for onset reports and {{< meta skill_recovered >}} for recovered.
The 90% interval of the joint forecast covered {{< meta coverage90_covered >}} of {{< meta coverage90_total >}} observations (@fig-evaluation A).
Every scored forecast predates the correction of the forecast defects reported in the Discussion, so the intervals scored here are wider than the model now produces. <!-- VERIFY: data/forecast_scores.csv was last refreshed in PR 637 -->

### Comparison with single-stream fits and published estimates

The single-stream fits disagreed on cumulative infections at the cut-off by a factor of {{< meta single_stream_ratio >}}, from {{< meta single_stream_min_median >}} for the {{< meta single_stream_min_fit >}} fit to {{< meta single_stream_max_median >}} for the {{< meta single_stream_max_fit >}} fit (@fig-evaluation B).
The joint estimate of {{< meta joint_median_unrounded >}} sat below the median of every single-stream fit ({{< meta single_stream_n_above_joint >}}), and its 90% interval of {{< meta cumulative_infections_interval90 >}} overlapped only the {{< meta single_stream_overlap_fits >}} intervals (@fig-evaluation B).

At the second cut-off of McCabe et al. [@mccabe2026; @mccabe2026lancet] the frozen joint interval overlapped the upper half of their back-calculation scenarios and the upper parts of their geographic-spread intervals (@fig-evaluation C).
At their third cut-off the frozen joint interval overlapped both sets of scenarios, and the back-calculation scenarios sat in its lower half (@fig-evaluation C).

The joint fit frozen at the calibration date of Chamla et al. [@chamla2026] projected {{< meta chamla_frozen_projection_median >}} confirmed cases (90% interval {{< meta chamla_frozen_projection_interval90 >}}) by their week-12 date, against their central {{< meta chamla_central_median >}} ({{< meta chamla_central_interval90 >}}) (@fig-evaluation D).
The observed count of {{< meta observed_confirmed_week12 >}} lay above their central projection and inside both their interval and the joint's (@fig-evaluation D).
